_comment: Registration for scripts/cpp-host-write.sh (issue #1139).
WHY THIS INSTRUMENT NEEDS A COMMITTED CASE (ADR 0008): it issues three
verdicts - 0 wrote, 3 deferred by request, 1 failed - and /cpp:init and
/cpp:update read the exit to decide whether to proceed, skip-and-say-so, or
stop. Neither re-derives whether the write happened. A wrong verdict here is
not a missed detection, it is CPP writing a surface a managed environment
asked it not to touch while reporting success.
THE ANCHOR IS NOT CONSTRUCTED. It is the code as it actually stood earlier in
this issue, one line restored: normalise() as `s="${s/#$HOME\//~/}"`, which
reads as 'replace a leading $HOME/ with ~/' and silently does nothing. Every
defer comparison then failed and the helper wrote the surface it was asked to
skip, exiting 0. The line had been read twice; one sandboxed run found it.
THE SPELLING IN THE BAD CASE IS THE WHOLE CASE. A defer spelled
"$HOME/.bashrc" matches by plain string equality even with normalisation
broken, so it cannot tell a working helper from the pre-fix one. Only the
MIXED spelling - caller says ~/.bashrc, helper resolves $HOME - discriminates.
Choosing the input that happens to pass is how a control proves nothing.
THE BAD PROBE CHECKS THE SURFACE, NOT THE VERDICT. A helper that exits 3
having written the file is the defect wearing the right answer, and the exit
code cannot see it. The probe fails the case if ~/.bashrc exists afterwards.
EACH PROBE RUNS IN ITS OWN mktemp $HOME and removes it on exit. The battery
substitutes {case} in place with no temp copy, so a gate that WRITES would
otherwise mutate its own committed fixture and stop being idempotent.
LIMITS. --no-guard is not a verdict; it exists only to preserve an unguarded
append across the relocation and belongs to #1142, so no case exercises it.
The six install-path helpers that reach outside $HOME are not observable at
all - see scripts/host-surface-check.py for why a PATH shim was rejected.

ANCHOR HASH NOTE: the anchor carries the same certified=authored downgrade as the live helper. It is vendored evidence of ONE defect - normalise() as a no-op - not a frozen snapshot of every unrelated string, and leaving the pre-downgrade value in it would have left the very string this change removes sitting in the tree, where a later absence check would trip on the text explaining the removal. The pin was recomputed deliberately rather than the edit skipped.

cases.name: bad-deferred-surface-written
cases.why: A defer request the helper must honour, spelled ~/.bashrc while the helper resolves $HOME. Correct verdict 3 with the surface absent; the pre-fix anchor exits 0 having written it.

cases.name: good-undeferred-write
cases.why: The ordinary path, no defer-set. Separates a working helper from one wedged at refuse-everything, which would score BAD on the bad case alone and look identical to a correct one.

anchors.why: VENDORED, not constructed: this is the real pre-fix code with normalise() restored verbatim. It MISSES bad-deferred-surface-written by writing the deferred surface and exiting 0 - a wrong verdict rather than a missed detection - and AGREES on good-undeferred-write, which keeps the demonstration isolated.
anchors.note: HASH RECOMPUTED DELIBERATELY. This anchor carries the same certified= downgrade as the live helper, so its bytes changed and the pin was recalculated. Defensible because the kind is vendored with a label rather than a real sha: there is no git-show claim for a recomputed hash to falsify, and provenance reads unverified structurally. An anchor is evidence of ONE defect - normalise() as a no-op - not a frozen snapshot of every unrelated string. The edit touches no byte that participates in the demonstration, and the battery was re-run afterwards: the anchor still misses the known-bad and still agrees on the known-good. A HISTORICAL anchor with a real sha must NOT be edited this way - the recomputed hash would make --verify-provenance read MISMATCH and the record would become a lie; there, the answer is a documented exclusion.
